newOrRepeatedLaterStageCategories.finding: The wrapper still ties video_pll.rst low. KEY0 resets downstream camera/logic but cannot restart a PLL that loses lock. This warning repeats the map-stage finding. Current configured operation and timing pass; arbitrary loss-of-lock recovery remains unverified.

Lite emits a LogicLock subscription warning with the inherited top partition preservation settings. This full source build uses no authored LogicLock placement region, reaches successful fit, and does not claim incremental preservation or licensed optimisation.

The detailed table lists missing drive-strength/slew assignments, not missing pad locations or I/O standards. Fitted output tables show the inherited defaults (16 mA, slew 1) for ordinary outputs; XCLK alone is explicitly 4 mA/slew 0. Pad locations and 3.3-V LVTTL remain assigned. This is an electrical-characterisation limit; no claim is made that defaults are optimal or that all output loads were measured.

No particular PLL output was nominated for compensation. The fitted PLL uses Normal mode/global feedback with the intended 25 MHz and 10 MHz outputs. Both derived clocks are present and routed timing passes. No external zero-phase requirement between the video and camera outputs is claimed.

The existing camera adapter returns PCLK on GPIO_1[21]/PIN_AJ24, which is not a dedicated global-clock input. Fitter routes it to CLKCTRL_G9. The physical pin cannot be changed without rewiring. Current PCLK input/register setup and hold pass the full routed four-corner gate; the warning is retained and no broad false path was added.

Intel SLD embedded SDC creates altera_reserved_tck at 30 MHz; project SDC redeclares it as 33.333 ns in fit and STA. This is the same intended rate to the specified precision. The final netlist has one named JTAG clock, and its internal setup/hold/recovery/removal checks pass. The duplicate definition warning remains visible.

The shared 36-bit GPIO inout bus has 31 permanently disabled output enables and four permanently enabled camera outputs; SIO_D is the remaining open-drain bidirectional signal. This matches the no-motion wrapper. It is not permission to drive chassis pins.
